headline: BRAVO MINING LUANGA PFS DELIVERS $1.45B NPV, 35% IRR — 393,800 OZ PGM+AU PER YEAR IN BRAZIL'S CARAJÁS
snippet: Bravo Mining Corp. (TSX-V: BRVO) released its independent Pre-Feasibility Study for the 100%-owned Luanga palladium + platinum + rhodium + gold + nickel deposit in Brazil's Carajás Mineral Province, delivering an after-tax NPV of US$1.45 billion at an 8% discount rate, a 35.1% IRR, and a 2.0-year payback — a 16% NPV improvement over the 2025 PEA driven by the switch to Jameson Cell flotation technology, which lifted PGM+Au concentrate recoveries from 80 to ~100 grams per tonne. The base case assumes 8.7 million tonnes processed annually over a 9.6-year mine life with average payable production of 393,800 oz PGM+Au plus 9,800 tonnes of nickel, generating $8.4 billion in net revenue and $2.8 billion in undiscounted free cash flow. A feasibility study is the next catalyst.

headline: CHINA GOLD IMPORTS BREACH 1,000 TONNES THROUGH AUGUST — PBOC ADDS 20.2T IN BIGGEST MONTHLY BUY SINCE 2023
snippet: China's official gold imports surpassed 1,000 metric tonnes through August 2026 — exceeding the full-year 2025 total with four months still to run — as a firmer yuan, slight domestic premiums and surging retail investment demand accelerated purchases, according to the latest customs data going back to 2017. The People's Bank of China added 20.2 metric tonnes to its reserves in August, its largest single-month purchase since October 2023, taking total PBOC gold reserves past 2,400 tonnes. For junior gold miners, the implication is structural: Chinese sovereign and retail demand has become a price floor that operates independently of Western futures positioning, materially shifting the downside scenarios that drive exploration company valuations.

headline: GLOBAL LITHIUM SOARS 50% AS UAE'S TITAN TABLES A$333M OFFER — 73% PREMIUM WITH A$120M MANNA LOAN FACILITY
snippet: Global Lithium Resources (ASX: GL1) accepted a unanimously board-recommended A$333-million ($237-million) cash takeover from UAE-headquartered Titan Australia Mining at A$1.15 per share — a 73% premium to the September 18 closing price of A$0.665 — sending shares up nearly 50% on Tuesday. Titan is building a vertically integrated business spanning lithium resources and downstream processing, and has committed a A$120-million loan facility for GL1's Manna hard-rock lithium project in Western Australia, with a Final Investment Decision targeted before year-end. The deal is the latest in a string of Gulf sovereign capital entering the Western Australian lithium supply chain and signals UAE industrial strategy shifting toward battery metal feedstock ownership.

headline: 7 MILLION OUNCES OF SILVER DRAINED FROM COMEX IN ONE WEEK — DELIVERY NOTICES POINT TO INSTITUTIONAL PHYSICAL PULL
snippet: Between September 10 and 17, silver held in COMEX depositories shrank by 7.1 million fine ounces to 330.1 million ounces — a drawdown 25% larger than the 5.75-million-ounce decline that opened the October 2025 squeeze — with the move driven almost entirely by the eligible (non-delivery-committed) category, which fell 8.6 million ounces to 232.8 million. Simultaneously, 6,168 delivery notices were filed for the front contract month through September 18, obligating the exchange to transfer 30.84 million ounces of physical metal. Analyst Mike Maharrey at Money Metals Exchange writes that a single week does not confirm a shortage, but if the outflow rate becomes a trend, the structural conditions for a repeat silver squeeze are already in place.

headline: DPM METALS DRILLS 716M AT 3.30 g/t AUEQ AT BREVENE SOUTH — PORPHYRY ENVELOPE EXCEEDS 500M × 500M IN BULGARIA
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) reported that delineation drill hole EX_BRES_555_02A returned 716.60 metres grading 3.30 g/t AuEq (1.63 g/t Au, 1.58% Cu, 17.09 g/t Mo) at the Brevene Porphyry South discovery in Bulgaria — where drilling has now confirmed a potassic alteration envelope exceeding 500 metres by 500 metres and more than 1,000 metres in vertical extent, with mineralisation extending onto the concession boundary of the adjacent Chelopech gold-copper mine. Up to eight high-capacity rigs are being dedicated to Brevene South with 15,000 additional metres planned through year-end, focused on delineating the northern and western extensions and testing depth potential. The scale of the alteration system is consistent with a significant bulk-tonnage copper-gold deposit adjacent to one of Southeast Europe's largest producing mines.

headline: REVIVAL GOLD MERCUR INFILL 64% DONE — 33.5M AT 0.92 g/t AU FROM 31M DEPTH IN UTAH HEAP LEACH TARGET
snippet: Revival Gold Inc. (TSX-V: RVG, OTCQX: RVLGF) reported results from 20 additional infill reverse-circulation holes at the Mercur Gold Project in Utah, headlined by 33.5 metres at 0.92 g/t Au from 31 metres in RM26-213, with 11,600 metres now complete across 119 holes — 64% of the year's program — and results continuing to support the grade and leachability estimates of the 2025 PEA. A fourth auger rig arrives at month-end to investigate legacy heap leach pad material; a Preliminary Feasibility Study is targeted for Q1 2027. Mercur is a permitted heap-leach-amenable deposit in a historically gold-producing Nevada-style system in Utah, and infill results confirming the PEA model systematically reduce resource-estimate risk ahead of a feasibility gate decision.

headline: MIDLAND AND SOQUEM FIND 26.8% COPPER BOULDERS IN LABRADOR TROUGH — NEW SHOWINGS EXPAND NACHICAPAU 4KM CORRIDOR
snippet: Midland Exploration Inc. (TSX-V: MD) and SOQUEM Inc. announced new copper, gold and silver boulder finds and outcrops at the Nachicapau project in Nunavik, Quebec, within a 4-km by 1.5-km copper-gold-silver corridor defined since 2022. New boulder samples reached 26.8% Cu, 0.87 g/t Au, and 238 g/t Ag (associated with digenite and malachite in monzonite-hosted veins), while two new outcrops returned up to 3.03% Cu, 0.77 g/t Au, 20.0 g/t Ag. The Labrador Trough — host to Glencore's massive Raglan nickel belt to the north — is emerging as one of Canada's least-explored polymetallic corridors, and boulder grades of 26.8% copper within a multi-kilometre anomaly confirm high-grade source rocks remain unlocated.

headline: KAZATOMPROM CUTS 2026 OUTPUT 10%, URANIUM TERM PRICE HITS ALL-TIME HIGH $96/LB — 'NO PRICE TRIGGERS ACCELERATION'
snippet: Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer, cut its 2026 nominal production capacity by roughly 10% — from 32,777 tU to 29,697 tU (~8 million lbs U3O8, approximately 5% of global supply) — and confirmed it has no intention of accelerating output regardless of spot price, explicitly validating a value-over-volume strategy. The cut coincides with long-term uranium contract prices reaching a nominal all-time record of US$96/lb on September 10, 2026, above the 2007 peak, while spot prices held near US$90/lb. Western utilities that under-contracted through 2023–2025 now face renewed term-market competition at record prices from a seller deliberately limiting supply, creating the tightest structural uranium backdrop since the early part of this decade.

headline: CATL'S JIANXIAWO MINE LOSES ENVIRONMENTAL APPROVAL — BENCHMARK CUTS 2026 LITHIUM OUTPUT FORECAST IN HALF
snippet: Chinese regulators revoked the environmental approval for CATL's Jianxiawo mine — China's largest lithium mine by capacity — after over 70 complaints from local residents, putting the operation back at square one on its environmental review process and effectively extending its shutdown potentially through Q4 2026 or into 2027. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence responded by cutting its 2026 mined output forecast for Jianxiawo from 62,500 tonnes LCE to 32,000 tonnes — a reduction of roughly 30,500 tonnes LCE, or approximately 12% of China's projected 2026 mine output. Combined with Global Lithium's Manna FID timeline and Mine Resources' Bald Hill restart still ramping, the loss of Jianxiawo's full-capacity contribution is the most significant supply-side shock to the lithium market in over a year.

headline: IRA EPSTEIN: GOLD AND SILVER SIDELINED AS EQUITIES RALLY — SUMMIT BINARY MAKES PRECIOUS METALS DIRECTIONAL WAGER
snippet: Ira Epstein's September 22 GoldSeek column notes that gold and silver were left out of Tuesday's broader equity market rally despite unexpected volume — a dynamic Epstein attributes to the Yom Kippur holiday thinning participants and the looming Trump-Xi summit on Thursday creating a directional bet rather than a hedge. With gold testing $4,307 support and the gold-silver ratio compressing as silver shows relative strength near $65-66/oz, Epstein argues the metals market is effectively in limbo until Thursday's summit resolves the rare earth delivery question and tariff truce status — making Thursday's outcome the single largest near-term variable for precious metals direction.
